newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers dip, rest of Europe steady to soft.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers dip, rest of Europe steady to soft.

text.p: European bunker prices dipped on Friday, losing part of Thursday's sharp gains as oil futures and fuel oil sagged, dealers said.
Rotterdam 380 CST traded in a range of $117/$119 fob by late afternoon, as barges dipped $1 to $116/$117.
ARA demand totalled 15-20,000 tonnes, including a single enquiry of about 7,000 tonnes, reportedly won by a major.
"We've seen reasonably healthy demand today," one supplier said.
Shipping problems due to frozen waterways lifted the normal Antwerp premium to almost $2 a tonne.
Hamburg bunkers responded in similar fashion, dipping by $1 to $123/$125 fob.
Mediterranean prices were steady to soft, with a few ports responding to Rotterdam's weakness.
Suppliers said Gibraltar was congested with a number of ships prepared to pick up up bunkers, but trading elsewhere was dormant.
Fujairah prices dipped by around $1 to $112/$113 fob, encouraging a large number of enquiries from shipowners recently back from New Year holidays.
